scenes.headline: How a state-space model decodes without writing its state
scenes.sub: Keep the last few inputs, and write the state once a window.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Bobbin! State-space layers keep a fixed-size memory, yet decoding copies it in and out on every token. Here is how to skip most of that.

scenes.text: Keep a checkpoint and the last few inputs, compute each output from them, and write the state only when the buffer fills.
scenes.mark: write the state only when the buffer fills
scenes.say: Keep an old checkpoint plus the last few inputs. Each output can be rebuilt from those, so the state is written only when the buffer fills.

steps.say: Each new token's inputs go into a small ring of recent records. On a normal step, nothing else is written.
The output comes from the checkpoint plus the ring, by dot products. The full state is never built.
Only when the ring is full are its inputs folded in, and the checkpoint written once.

left.title: Snapshot every draft
items: One full state written per draft
left.say: For speculative decoding, the usual fix saves a state copy after every draft, because a summary cannot be undone.

right.title: Replay the drafts
items: Drafts are just records in the ring
Reject them by moving a pointer
right.say: Here the drafts are just records. Rejecting one moves a pointer back.

scenes.title: Why a rounded state drifts
scenes.say: Now precision. Round a shared state every step, and its error follows this recurrence.

parts.note: every past rounding is carried forward
parts.say: Every past rounding stays in the state, decayed but never removed.

parts.note: a new rounding on each update
parts.say: A separate read copy is never fed back, so each output sees one rounding of a clean state.

steps.say: On a small Qwen model, a shared four-bit state drifts upward with length. The separate copy stays flat.
At the longest length, the error is thirty-six times smaller.

scenes.title: Plain decoding at batch 256
scenes.note: speedup over a tuned vLLM; none at batch 1
scenes.say: Halving the writes speeds up a whole decode step by up to one and a half times at large batch. At batch one, nothing.

scenes.text: Most steps need an output, not a state: that halves traffic, frees rollback and keeps rounding out of the loop.
scenes.mark: Most steps need an output, not a state
scenes.say: Most decode steps need an output, not a state. That halves traffic, frees rollback, and keeps rounding out of the loop.

recap: Cache inputs, write the state once a window
The read copy never feeds back
scenes.say: Cache the inputs, roll back with a pointer, never feed the coarse copy back.
